description: An information-discovery profile for muscular dystrophy and evidence-supported major subtypes. It surfaces public trials, publication metadata, and strictly relevant headlines; it does not provide medical advice, recommend studies or treatments, assess eligibility, or interpret findings.

synopsis.overview: Muscular dystrophy describes a group of genetic conditions that cause progressive muscle weakness. Different gene changes produce different types, including Duchenne, Becker, myotonic, facioscapulohumeral and limb-girdle muscular dystrophies.
synopsis.manifestations: Weakness may begin in childhood or adulthood and can affect walking, lifting, balance and joints. The pattern and speed vary by type; some forms also affect the heart, breathing muscles, spine, eyes or other organs.
synopsis.management: There is no cure for most forms. Type-specific multidisciplinary care may include physiotherapy, mobility and occupational support, medicines that slow progression in some conditions, respiratory support, cardiac monitoring and treatment, and surgery for selected complications.
synopsis.outlook: The outlook ranges widely between types and individuals. Some forms progress slowly with a near-normal lifespan, while others cause early loss of mobility or serious heart and breathing complications and can shorten life. Genetic diagnosis helps guide monitoring and counselling.
